secret.name: fda028_limiter_epoch_key
secret.generation: on-server gen_random_bytes(64); the value never left the database and was never printed, logged, or written to source or receipt
secret.encoding: lowercase hex, 128 characters, no whitespace, decodes to exactly 64 bytes

correctionMadeBeforeItCouldBite.what: first provisioned base64 (89 chars — Postgres's encode(...,'base64') line-wraps at 76, so the value even carried a newline)
correctionMadeBeforeItCouldBite.whyWrong: limiter.current_epoch_key does decode(v_txt,'hex') and its rotate path writes encode(p_key,'hex'). A base64 value would have raised on first use, and the newline would have been silent key material.
correctionMadeBeforeItCouldBite.howFound: read the limiter source to check how it consumes the secret before moving on, rather than assuming any random string would do
correctionMadeBeforeItCouldBite.fix: vault.update_secret in place with encode(gen_random_bytes(64),'hex'); verified it now decodes to 64 bytes exactly as the function will decode it

clientRoleIsolation.empiricalAsRealRoles: anon -> ERROR permission denied for schema vault; authenticated -> ERROR permission denied for schema vault
clientRoleIsolation.note: the first empirical attempt used SET LOCAL ROLE outside a transaction, which only warns — it read as postgres and would have been a false negative. Re-run inside a transaction with current_user asserted.

step3_webhook.reasoning: the accepted design fails closed when no endpoint is configured, and that is the property worth proving on staging. Configuring an endpoint merely to make a delivery test green would prove less and risk pointing a disposable branch at something real.
step3_webhook.productionEndpointFallback: none — there is no default in the candidate
step3_webhook.webhookSecretOnBranch: absent, so the function fails closed at the secret check as well
step3_webhook.stagingEndpointAvailableIfLaterNeeded: the branch has its own notify-flag-status Edge Function at https://cepayqmsoqxshsiyqnvz.supabase.co/functions/v1/notify-flag-status — a staging-scoped endpoint exists and would never be production
